title: How to use virtual machines

note: Pre-existing committed customize-workshops index adopted as the basis; no one has edited it. The draft adds the toctree entry for the new VM how-to.

steps.text: Record the Workshop and LXD versions this procedure is verified against
Query LXD for the disk shift capability that decides whether a VM workshop can carry SDKs
Launch a VM workshop before opting in, capturing the refusal and its opt-in hint
Set the workshop.experimental-vms snap setting and restart the workshop daemon
Create a VM workshop definition with workshop init --vm and show the generated YAML
Launch the VM workshop
Confirm the virtual-machine confinement with workshop info
Add an SDK to the definition and refresh, capturing the refusal that SDKs are unavailable for virtual machines
Change the definition to container confinement and refresh, capturing the refusal that confinement changed
Stop and start the VM workshop, confirming the lifecycle operations the page summarizes
Remove the demo VM workshop

{'claim': 'A virtual machine consumes more memory and disk than a container.', 'why': 'Not measured during the walk. {'claim': 'The first launch on a given base downloads a virtual machine image.', 'why': 'The walk launched against an already cached virtual machine image, so the download itself was not observed. audience: Existing Workshop users who already run container workshops daily and have hit an isolation or nesting wall (harder boundary around an AI agent, or running LXD containers and VMs inside a workshop). Readers still evaluating which runtime to pick are pointed back to containers.
title: How to use virtual machines

steps.text: On the Workshop build that predates the runtime key, create a VM workshop with workshop init --vm and launch it, so a VM from an earlier version exists to carry forward
Refresh the workshop snap to the latest/edge revision that carries the runtime key, then turn the experimental VM setting off and restart the daemon so the opt-in refusal can be captured again
Record the Workshop and LXD versions this procedure is verified against, and that workshop init now offers the runtime option
Query LXD for the disk shift capability that decides whether a VM workshop can carry SDKs
Read workshop info for the VM launched before the upgrade, capturing the runtime it now reports
Replace the confinement key in the earlier VM's definition with runtime: lxd-vm and refresh, capturing the refusal, then remove that workshop
Launch a new definition that still carries confinement: virtual-machine, capturing from workshop info that it runs as a container, then remove it
Create a throwaway definition with workshop init --runtime lxd-vm and launch it before opting in, capturing the refusal and its opt-in hint
Set the workshop.experimental-vms snap setting and restart the workshop daemon
Create a VM workshop definition with workshop init --runtime lxd-vm and show the generated YAML
Launch the VM workshop
Confirm the lxd-vm runtime with workshop info
Add an SDK to the definition and refresh, capturing the refusal that SDKs are unavailable for virtual machines
Change the definition to runtime: lxd-container and refresh, capturing the refusal that the runtime changed
Restore the definition to runtime: lxd-vm without SDKs, then stop and start the VM workshop, reading workshop info after each
Remove the demo VM workshop

command: cd .dogen/staging/use-virtual-machines/scratch && workshop --version && lxc version && workshop init --help
output_excerpt:
0.9.7
Client version: 6.9
Server version: 6.9

Create a new workshop definition file in the project's .workshop/ directory.

The NAME argument sets the workshop name. The command creates a named
workshop file at .workshop/<NAME>.yaml. This fails if a workshop with
the same name already exists.

The supported bases are ubuntu@22.04, ubuntu@24.04, and ubuntu@26.04.
The supported runtimes are lxd-container (the default) and lxd-vm.

SDKs are specified as a comma-separated list. Each SDK entry can optionally
include a channel using the <NAME>/<CHANNEL> syntax (e.g., "go/1.26/stable").

Usage:
  workshop init <NAME> [flags]

Examples:

Create a workshop called "dev" with the Go and UV SDKs:
$ workshop init dev --sdks go,uv

Create a workshop with a specific SDK channel:
$ workshop init dev --sdks go/1.26/stable

Create a workshop using a specific base:
$ workshop init dev --base ubuntu@22.04 --sdks go

Flags:
      --base string      Base image for the workshop. (default "ubuntu@24.04")
      --runtime string   Sandbox technology to use. (default "lxd-container")
      --sdks strings     Comma-separated list of SDKs (e.g., "go,uv/latest/stable").

Global Flags:
  -h, --help             Print the help message for the command.
  -p, --project string   Specify the project's directory path. (default "/home/artem.konev@canonical.com/Documents/workshop-akcano/.dogen/staging/use-virtual-machines/scratch")
  -v, --version          Print Workshop version.
